correctness.rationale: Counting the crossing unordered bonds gives 2 min(r,n) at separation r, each of excess energy 2J_r; the field contribution is −2hn. The increment divided by 4J is T(n)−1/R with T(n)=sum_{r>n} r^(−1−sigma). Strict decrease handles ties. Integral upper/lower bounds on T at n and n−1 yield |n−(R/sigma)^(1/sigma)|<1 whenever a maximizing n is at least 2, which holds eventually uniformly on compact lambda sets. Euler–Maclaurin on the finite harmonic sum and the tail has a uniform remainder for sigma in [1/2,3/2] after subtracting the pole; the two terms of order n^(−sigma) cancel. The smooth energy has derivative n^(−sigma)/sigma−1/R and second derivative −n^(−1−sigma), so replacing the discrete optimum by x* costs O(x*^(−1−sigma)). At x*, the tail and field give zeta(sigma)−x*^(1−sigma)/(sigma−1). Writing the pole-subtracted power as log(x*) times the integral of exp(−t(sigma−1)log(x*)) on [0,1] makes the expansion uniform through zero. Inserting log(x*)=ell−lambda+O_K(ell^−1) gives the finite part gamma−lambda exp(−lambda) and both length estimates. Phi is positive and has strictly negative derivative by its integral representation. Applies only to optimized contiguous-interval energy in the infinite chain at fixed J and compact lambda, not to kinetics or general saddles.
